name: print-scheduler
title: Print Scheduler
description:
Pick a sliced file that is already on the printer, pick when it should start, and the printer starts it for you at that time.

The scheduler refuses far more often than it starts. It will not start a job on a printer that is not idle, it will not start a job whose time has already passed, and it records a reason for every job it did not start. It cannot see the bed, so the person scheduling a job is the one promising the bed will be clear.
tagline: Start a print at a time you choose.
author: Mauker

variables.name: START_TOLERANCE_MINUTES
variables.description: How many minutes late a job may still start. It is a retry budget for a printer that is briefly unreachable, not permission to start late.

variables.name: SETTLED_JOBS_KEPT
variables.description: How many finished and cancelled jobs to show in the list. Older ones are dropped from the list automatically. Nothing scheduled is ever dropped.

config.label: Minutes a job may start late
config.hint: A job noticed within this many minutes of its time still starts. Past it, the job is cancelled and the reason is recorded. A printer that is busy is never waited for, whatever this is set to.

config.label: Finished jobs to keep
config.hint: The list of settled jobs is trimmed to this many, newest first, so it does not grow forever. Jobs that have not run yet are never dropped. This only changes how many rows you see: the scheduler keeps enough history of its own to tell a levelled print's setup time from an unlevelled one, whatever this is set to.

attributions:
# Attributions - print-scheduler

**Plugin author:** Mauker

This plugin ships no third-party code.

The idea, and the two warnings it is built to answer, come from jneilliii's OctoPrint-PrintScheduler
(https://github.com/jneilliii/OctoPrint-PrintScheduler, AGPL-3.0). No code from it is used here: that
plugin targets OctoPrint and this one targets Klipper through Moonraker.

The nginx authentication subrequest follows the pattern established by the Bespok3d plugin
`u1-remote-screen`, whose own location file credits paxx12's Extended Firmware overlay
`61-app-remote-screen` (GPL-3.0). The block here is written against Moonraker's documented
`/access/user` endpoint rather than copied.
